content.title: Is Your Toothpaste Safe?
content.subtitle: Microplastics, Oral Health & the Sunnah
content.body:
We use toothpaste every day to keep our teeth and mouth clean. But what if it contains tiny plastic particles invisible to the naked eye? These are known as microplastics.

Microplastics Found in Toothpaste

A year-long study by the Environment and Social Development Organization (ESDO) tested 34 toothpaste samples from 19 local and international brands available in Bangladesh. Microplastics were detected in 26 samples, or 76.5%. Four out of six samples marketed for children also contained microplastics.

Should We Be Concerned?

Microplastics are plastic particles smaller than 5 millimeters. They can enter the body through food, water, and air, and have already been detected in human blood, lungs, placenta, and other biological samples.

Their long-term health effects are still being studied. However, research has raised concerns about potential effects such as inflammation, oxidative stress, and hormonal disruption.

What Does the Sunnah Teach Us?

Islam offers a simple practice for oral hygiene: Miswak. The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ placed great importance on it.

He ﷺ said, “Miswak is a means of purification for the mouth and a means of pleasing the Lord.” (Sunan an-Nasa’i: 5)

In another hadith, the Prophet ﷺ said, “If I had not feared that it would be difficult for my Ummah, I would have commanded them to use the miswak before every prayer.” (Sahih al-Bukhari: 887; Sahih Muslim: 252)

A Sunnah with Recognized Benefits

Modern research also suggests that proper Miswak use may help reduce dental plaque and gingival inflammation, with some studies reporting results comparable to conventional toothbrushes.

So, alongside being mindful of what we use for oral care, we can reconnect with this beautiful Sunnah.

Let oral hygiene revive a Sunnah and turn a simple daily habit into a means of seeking Allah’s pleasure.
